readerCopy.body: A boundary can lose its meaning when a clear no is immediately followed by an apology that quietly negotiates it away. When Mars squares Chiron, action and sensitivity create friction, making assertion collide with the learned fear that anger, refusal, or taking up space will cost approval. If you notice yourself apologizing immediately after saying no, the discomfort may be changing the answer before the actual consequence has appeared. A boundary becomes easier to evaluate once it remains intact long enough to show what happens next.
